new_statements.rule_in_words: Smythe classes Mokerang in his Group 3 (all Manus-network languages); for Group 3 as a whole the 'main position of accent' is the final syllable (vs penultimate in Aua-Wuvulu and initial in Seimat/Kaniet), with 'mixed' rhythm and tone reported in some dialects. This is a group-level typological generalisation from Smythe's own 1946-48/1958 survey samples, not a Mokerang-specific description; 'main position' implies a predominant, not exceptionless, final accent.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Mokerang. The wording 'main position' signals a tendency; Smythe's own detailed note on another Group 3 language (Gele'/Kele, fn.13 p.1232) says stress there is phonemic but tends to fall on long vowels, reduplicated penults and otherwise final syllables, and Hamel 1994 finds the sister language Loniu has non-lexical penultimate-or-final stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Group-level statement (Smythe's Group 3 = c. 20 Manus languages, Mokerang explicitly enumerated at p.1214); presumably word-level accent in citation forms from 195-item vocabulary samples plus sentences; no discussion of word vs phrase domain.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is not Mokerang-specific: it is Smythe's Table 1 value for his whole Group 3 (all Manus-network languages), in which Mokerang is explicitly listed (p.1214, Group 3 B.I Family 1a 'Mokerang, Papitalai, Drangot, Labahan, Bowat, Loniu'). Smythe (1970) and Healey (1976a) treat Mokareng and Papitalai (papi1254; Cleary-Kemp's 'Koro', cf. koro1316) as one language, whereas Ross 1988 and Glottolog pair Mokerang with Loniu (loni1238) and keep Papitalai/Koro separate; Hamel 1994:20-21 fn.5 reports Loniu speakers call the speech of Mokoreng village 'Koro'. No dedicated phonological description of Mokerang exists in print; Blust never sampled it.

sources.note: Table 1 (p.1211) 'main position of accent': Group 1 penultimate, Group 2 initial, Group 3 final; Group 3 'rhythm: mixed type', 'tones: + in some dialects'. p.1214 places Mokerang in Group 3 (Subgroup B.I, Family 1a: Mokerang, Papitalai, Drangot, Labahan, Bowat, Loniu). Group-level generalisation by the fieldworker who collected the Mokareng sample; no Mokerang-specific prose on accent.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2021. Eight Languages of the Admiralty Islands, Papua New Guinea. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia Special Issue 2021 (front matter/introduction and Sketch 6: Loniu).
sources.note: Mokerang is not among the 26 languages Blust sampled in 1975 (Table 0.1) and is not one of the eight sketches; zero mentions of Mokerang/Mokoreng. Loniu sketch defers to Hamel on stress and notes penultimate stress in free nominal bases vs final in singular possessed forms.

sources.citation: Hamel, Patricia J. 1994. A grammar and lexicon of Loniu, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-103. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: About Loniu (loni1238, Mokerang's closest relative), sec. 2.5.1 pp.23-25: 'Stress does not appear to be a lexically differential feature in Loniu. It is either penultimate or final, but varies or shifts according to the structure of the phrase or clause'. Mokoreng appears only as the neighbouring village/language (pp.1, 20-21 fn.5); nothing on Mokerang phonology.
